from enum import Enum
from typing import Optional


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Enums and Exceptions
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

class ClaimStatus(Enum):
    RECEIVED = "RECEIVED"
    VALIDATED = "VALIDATED"
    REJECTED = "REJECTED"
    DENIED = "DENIED"
    APPROVED = "APPROVED"
    PARTIALLY_APPROVED = "PARTIALLY_APPROVED"
    APPEALED = "APPEALED"
    APPEAL_APPROVED = "APPEAL_APPROVED"
    APPEAL_DENIED = "APPEAL_DENIED"
    PAID = "PAID"


class DenialReason(Enum):
    NONE = "NONE"
    INVALID_FORMAT = "INVALID_FORMAT"
    MEMBER_NOT_ELIGIBLE = "MEMBER_NOT_ELIGIBLE"
    PROVIDER_NOT_CREDENTIALED = "PROVIDER_NOT_CREDENTIALED"
    SERVICE_NOT_COVERED = "SERVICE_NOT_COVERED"
    PRIOR_AUTH_REQUIRED = "PRIOR_AUTH_REQUIRED"
    DUPLICATE_CLAIM = "DUPLICATE_CLAIM"
    TIMELY_FILING_EXCEEDED = "TIMELY_FILING_EXCEEDED"
    BENEFIT_MAX_EXCEEDED = "BENEFIT_MAX_EXCEEDED"


class ClaimAdjudicationError(Exception):
    """Base exception for adjudication failures."""
    pass


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data Models
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

@dataclass
class Claim:
    claim_id: str
    member_id: str
    provider_id: str
    service_code: str
    diagnosis_code: str
    service_date: str          # ISO format YYYY-MM-DD
    billed_amount: float
    submission_date: str = field(default_factory=lambda: datetime.date.today().isoformat())
    prior_auth_number: Optional[str] = None
    place_of_service: str = "11"
    status: ClaimStatus = ClaimStatus.RECEIVED
    denial_reason: DenialReason = DenialReason.NONE
    notes: list = field(default_factory=list)


@dataclass
class Member:
    member_id: str
    name: str
    active: bool
    eligibility_start: str
    eligibility_end: str
    plan_id: str
    deductible_remaining: float
    out_of_pocket_max_remaining: float
    coinsurance_rate: float = 0.20  # member's coinsurance percentage


@dataclass
class Provider:
    provider_id: str
    name: str
    credentialed: bool
    credential_expiry: str
    in_network: bool
    npi: str


@dataclass
class CoverageRule:
    service_code: str
    covered: bool
    requires_prior_auth: bool
    allowed_amount: float
    annual_benefit_max: Optional[float] = None
    copay: float = 0.0


@dataclass
class AdjudicationResult:
    claim_id: str
    status: ClaimStatus
    denial_reason: DenialReason
    allowed_amount: float = 0.0
    member_responsibility: float = 0.0
    plan_payment: float = 0.0
    eob: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
    messages: list = field(default_factory=list)


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# In-memory financial ledger (simulating a financial records system)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

class FinancialLedger:
    def __init__(self):
        self.transactions = []
        self.member_ytd_paid = {}
        self.provider_ytd_paid = {}

    def record_payment(self, claim_id, member_id, provider_id, amount, txn_type="PAYMENT"):
        txn = {
            "transaction_id": str(uuid.uuid4()),
            "claim_id": claim_id,
            "member_id": member_id,
            "provider_id": provider_id,
            "amount": amount,
            "type": txn_type,
            "timestamp": datetime.datetime.utcnow().isoformat(),
        }
        self.transactions.append(txn)
        self.member_ytd_paid[member_id] = self.member_ytd_paid.get(member_id, 0.0) + amount
        self.provider_ytd_paid[provider_id] = self.provider_ytd_paid.get(provider_id, 0.0) + amount
        return txn


# Global ledger + duplicate-claim tracker + service benefit usage tracker
_LEDGER = FinancialLedger()
_PROCESSED_CLAIM_KEYS = set()
_ANNUAL_BENEFIT_USED = {}  # (member_id, service_code) -> amount used this year


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Validation Helpers
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

def _parse_date(date_str):
    try:
        return datetime.date.fromisoformat(date_str)
    except (ValueError, TypeError):
        return None


def validate_claim_format(claim: Claim) -> list:
    """Validates structural correctness of a claim. Returns a list of errors."""
    errors = []

    if not claim.claim_id or not re.match(r"^[A-Za-z0-9\-]{5,40}$", claim.claim_id):
        errors.append("Invalid claim_id format.")

    if not claim.member_id or not re.match(r"^[A-Za-z0-9]{4,20}$", claim.member_id):
        errors.append("Invalid member_id format.")

    if not claim.provider_id or not re.match(r"^[A-Za-z0-9]{4,20}$", claim.provider_id):
        errors.append("Invalid provider_id format.")

    if not claim.service_code or not re.match(r"^[A-Za-z0-9]{3,10}$", claim.service_code):
        errors.append("Invalid service_code format.")

    if not claim.diagnosis_code or not re.match(r"^[A-Za-z0-9\.]{3,10}$", claim.diagnosis_code):
        errors.append("Invalid diagnosis_code format.")

    service_date = _parse_date(claim.service_date)
    if not service_date:
        errors.append("Invalid service_date format; expected YYYY-MM-DD.")
    else:
        if service_date > datetime.date.today():
            errors.append("Service date cannot be in the future.")

    submission_date = _parse_date(claim.submission_date)
    if not submission_date:
        errors.append("Invalid submission_date format; expected YYYY-MM-DD.")

    if service_date and submission_date:
        filing_days = (submission_date - service_date).days
        if filing_days > 365:
            errors.append("TIMELY_FILING_EXCEEDED")

    if claim.billed_amount is None or claim.billed_amount <= 0:
        errors.append("Billed amount must be a positive number.")

    if claim.place_of_service and not re.match(r"^\d{2}$", claim.place_of_service):
        errors.append("Invalid place_of_service code.")

    return errors


def check_duplicate_claim(claim: Claim) -> bool:
    """Returns True if a claim with same key attributes has already been processed."""
    key = (claim.member_id, claim.provider_id, claim.service_code, claim.service_date, round(claim.billed_amount, 2))
    if key in _PROCESSED_CLAIM_KEYS:
        return True
    return False


def _register_claim_key(claim: Claim):
    key = (claim.member_id, claim.provider_id, claim.service_code, claim.service_date, round(claim.billed_amount, 2))
    _PROCESSED_CLAIM_KEYS.add(key)


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Eligibility & Credentialing
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

def verify_member_eligibility(member: Optional[Member], claim: Claim) -> bool:
    if member is None:
        return False
    if not member.active:
        return False

    service_date = _parse_date(claim.service_date)
    elig_start = _parse_date(member.eligibility_start)
    elig_end = _parse_date(member.eligibility_end)

    if not (service_date and elig_start and elig_end):
        return False

    return elig_start <= service_date <= elig_end


def check_provider_credentials(provider: Optional[Provider], claim: Claim) -> bool:
    if provider is None:
        return False
    if not provider.credentialed:
        return False

    service_date = _parse_date(claim.service_date)
    expiry = _parse_date(provider.credential_expiry)

    if not (service_date and expiry):
        return False

    return service_date <= expiry


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Coverage Rules & Payment Calculation
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

def apply_coverage_rules(claim: Claim, rule: Optional[CoverageRule]) -> tuple:
    """
    Determines whether the claim is covered given plan rules.
    Returns (is_covered: bool, denial_reason: DenialReason, allowed_amount: float)
    """
    if rule is None or not rule.covered:
        return False, DenialReason.SERVICE_NOT_COVERED, 0.0

    if rule.requires_prior_auth and not claim.prior_auth_number:
        return False, DenialReason.PRIOR_AUTH_REQUIRED, 0.0

    if rule.annual_benefit_max is not None:
        used = _ANNUAL_BENEFIT_USED.get((claim.member_id, claim.service_code), 0.0)
        if used >= rule.annual_benefit_max:
            return False, DenialReason.BENEFIT_MAX_EXCEEDED, 0.0

    allowed_amount = min(rule.allowed_amount, claim.billed_amount)
    return True, DenialReason.NONE, allowed_amount


def calculate_payment(claim: Claim, member: Member, rule: CoverageRule, allowed_amount: float) -> dict:
    """
    Calculates plan payment vs. member responsibility, applying deductible,
    copay, coinsurance, and out-of-pocket max logic.
    """
    remaining_allowed = allowed_amount
    member_deductible_portion = 0.0

    # Apply deductible
    if member.deductible_remaining > 0:
        member_deductible_portion = min(member.deductible_remaining, remaining_allowed)
        remaining_allowed -= member_deductible_portion
        member.deductible_remaining -= member_deductible_portion

    # Apply flat copay (charged in addition, capped by remaining allowed amount)
    copay = min(rule.copay, remaining_allowed) if rule.copay else 0.0
    remaining_allowed -= copay

    # Apply coinsurance to what's left
    coinsurance_amount = round(remaining_allowed * member.coinsurance_rate, 2)
    plan_payment = round(remaining_allowed - coinsurance_amount, 2)

    member_responsibility = round(member_deductible_portion + copay + coinsurance_amount, 2)

    # Enforce out-of-pocket max
    if member.out_of_pocket_max_remaining <= 0:
        # Member has met OOP max; plan covers remainder, no member charge
        shift_to_plan = member_responsibility
        plan_payment = round(plan_payment + shift_to_plan, 2)
        member_responsibility = 0.0
    elif member_responsibility > member.out_of_pocket_max_remaining:
        overage = round(member_responsibility - member.out_of_pocket_max_remaining, 2)
        member_responsibility = member.out_of_pocket_max_remaining
        plan_payment = round(plan_payment + overage, 2)
        member.out_of_pocket_max_remaining = 0.0
    else:
        member.out_of_pocket_max_remaining = round(member.out_of_pocket_max_remaining - member_responsibility, 2)

    # Track annual benefit usage
    key = (claim.member_id, claim.service_code)
    _ANNUAL_BENEFIT_USED[key] = _ANNUAL_BENEFIT_USED.get(key, 0.0) + allowed_amount

    return {
        "allowed_amount": round(allowed_amount, 2),
        "deductible_applied": round(member_deductible_portion, 2),
        "copay_applied": round(copay, 2),
        "coinsurance_applied": round(coinsurance_amount, 2),
        "plan_payment": round(plan_payment, 2),
        "member_responsibility": round(member_responsibility, 2),
    }


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# EOB Generation
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

def generate_eob(claim: Claim, payment_breakdown: dict, status: ClaimStatus,
                  denial_reason: DenialReason) -> dict:
    eob = {
        "eob_id": str(uuid.uuid4()),
        "claim_id": claim.claim_id,
        "member_id": claim.member_id,

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

def handle_appeal(original_result: AdjudicationResult, appeal_reason: str,
                   supporting_docs_provided: bool, rule: Optional[CoverageRule],
                   member: Optional[Member], claim: Claim) -> AdjudicationResult:
    """
    Handles an appeal for a previously denied/partially approved claim.
    An appeal can succeed if valid supporting documentation is provided and
    the underlying issue is resolvable (e.g., prior auth obtained retroactively,
    eligibility corrected, or coverage rule reconsidered).
    """
    if original_result.status not in (ClaimStatus.DENIED, ClaimStatus.REJECTED,
                                       ClaimStatus.PARTIALLY_APPROVED):
        original_result.messages.append("Appeal not applicable: claim was not denied or rejected.")
        return original_result

    claim.status = ClaimStatus.APPEALED

            original_result.plan_payment = breakdown["plan_payment"]
            original_result.member_responsibility = breakdown["member_responsibility"]
            original_result.eob = generate_eob(claim, breakdown, ClaimStatus.APPEAL_APPROVED, DenialReason.NONE)
            claim.status = ClaimStatus.APPEAL_APPROVED
            _LEDGER.record_payment(claim.claim_id, claim.member_id, claim.provider_id,
                                    breakdown["plan_payment"], txn_type="APPEAL_PAYMENT")
            original_result.messages.append("Appeal approved: prior authorization documentation accepted.")
        else:
            original_result.status = ClaimStatus.APPEAL_DENIED
            claim.status = ClaimStatus.APPEAL_DENIED
            original_result.messages.append("Appeal denied: service not covered under plan.")

    elif original_result.denial_reason == DenialReason.MEMBER_NOT_ELIGIBLE:
        original_result.status = ClaimStatus.APPEAL_DENIED
        claim.status = ClaimStatus.APPEAL_DENIED

    elif original_result.denial_reason in (DenialReason.SERVICE_NOT_COVERED,
                                             DenialReason.BENEFIT_MAX_EXCEEDED,
                                             DenialReason.TIMELY_FILING_EXCEEDED,
                                             DenialReason.INVALID_FORMAT,
                                             DenialReason.PROVIDER_NOT_CREDENTIALED,
                                             DenialReason.DUPLICATE_CLAIM):
        original_result.status = ClaimStatus.APPEAL_DENIED
        claim.status = ClaimStatus.APPEAL_DENIED

            f"Appeal denied: {original_result.denial_reason.value} could not be overturned with provided documentation."

    else:

        original_result.messages.append("Appeal denied: no valid basis to overturn decision.")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Financial Records Update
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

def update_financial_records(claim: Claim, result: AdjudicationResult):
    if result.status in (ClaimStatus.APPROVED, ClaimStatus.PARTIALLY_APPROVED,
                          ClaimStatus.APPEAL_APPROVED):
        _LEDGER.record_payment(
            claim.claim_id, claim.member_id, claim.provider_id,
            result.plan_payment, txn_type="PAYMENT"
        )
        claim.status = ClaimStatus.PAID
        result.messages.append("Financial records updated; payment issued to provider.")
    else:
        result.messages.append("No payment issued; financial records updated with denial entry.")
        _LEDGER.record_payment(
            claim.claim_id, claim.member_id, claim.provider_id,
            0.0, txn_type="DENIAL"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Main Adjudication Function
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

def adjudicate_claim(

    """

    result = AdjudicationResult(

    format_errors = validate_claim_format(claim)

        else:

    # Step 2: Check for duplicate claim
    if check_duplicate_claim(claim):
        claim.status = ClaimStatus.DENIED

        result.denial_reason = DenialReason.DUPLICATE_CLAIM

    if not verify_member_eligibility(member, claim):

        result.denial_reason = DenialReason.MEMBER_NOT_ELIGIBLE

    result.messages.append("Member eligibility verified.")

    # Step 4: Check provider credentials
    if not check_provider_credentials(provider, claim):
        claim.status = ClaimStatus.DENIED
        result.status = ClaimStatus.DENIED
        result.denial_reason = DenialReason.PROVIDER_NOT_CREDENTIALED
        result.messages.append("Claim denied: provider not credentialed on service date.")

    result.messages.append("Provider credentials verified.")

    # Step 5: Apply coverage rules
    is_covered, denial_reason, allowed_amount = apply_coverage_rules(claim, coverage_rule)
    if not is_covered:
        claim.status = ClaimStatus.DENIED
        result.status = ClaimStatus.DENIED
        result.denial_reason = denial_reason
        result.messages.append(f"Claim denied: {denial_reason.value}.")

        update_financial_records(claim, result)

        if appeal_request:
            result = handle_appeal(
                result,

                appeal_request.get("supporting_docs_provided", False),
                coverage_rule,

    # Step 6: Calculate payment
    payment_breakdown = calculate_payment(claim, member, coverage_rule, allowed_amount)

    # Determine final status: full vs partial approval
    if payment_breakdown["plan_payment"] <= 0 and payment_breakdown["member_responsibility"] > 0:
        result.status = ClaimStatus.PARTIALLY_APPROVED
    elif payment_breakdown["allowed_amount"] < claim.billed_amount:
        result.status = ClaimStatus.PARTIALLY_APPROVED
    else:
        result.status = ClaimStatus.APPROVED

    claim.status = result.status
    result.denial_reason = DenialReason.NONE
    result.allowed_amount = payment_breakdown["allowed_amount"]
    result.plan_payment = payment_breakdown["plan_payment"]
    result.member_responsibility = payment_breakdown["member_responsibility"]

    # Step 7: Generate EOB
    result.eob = generate_eob(claim, payment_breakdown, result.status, result.denial_reason)
    result.messages.append("EOB generated.")

    # Step 8: Update financial records
    update_financial_records(claim, result)
    _register_claim_key(claim)

    # Step 9: Handle appeal if simultaneously requested (e.g., partial approval dispute)
    if appeal_request:
        result = handle_appeal(
            result,
            appeal_request.get("appeal_reason", ""),
            appeal_request.get("supporting_docs_provided", False),
            coverage_rule,
            member,
            claim,
        )

    return result

DOCUMENTATION: MARKET MICROSTRUCTURE OVERVIEW
------------------------------------------------
This module implements a simplified market-making strategy that reacts to
order book imbalances and trade flow. Below is background documentation
on the microstructure concepts this algorithm relies on:

1. LIMIT ORDER BOOK (LOB)
   The LOB is a two-sided queue of resting orders: bids (buy orders) and
   asks (sell orders), each sorted by price-time priority. The best bid
   is the highest price a buyer is willing to pay; the best ask is the
   lowest price a seller is willing to accept. The difference between
   them is the BID-ASK SPREAD, which compensates liquidity providers for
   inventory and adverse selection risk.

2. PRICE-TIME PRIORITY
   Orders at the same price level are filled in the order they arrived
   (FIFO). This means being "first in the queue" at a price level has
   real economic value, since you get filled before others at the same
   price when a matching order arrives.

3. ORDER BOOK IMBALANCE (OBI)
   OBI = (BidVolume - AskVolume) / (BidVolume + AskVolume)
   A positive imbalance (more resting bid volume) is often interpreted as
   short-term buying pressure, since it suggests more participants are
   willing to buy at current levels than sell. This is a weak but
   commonly used short-horizon predictive signal.

4. ADVERSE SELECTION
   Market makers quoting on both sides risk being "picked off" by
   informed traders right before the price moves against their quote.
   Wider spreads and quote skewing (based on inventory or OBI) are
   common defenses.

5. LATENCY AND RACE CONDITIONS
   In real trading systems, multiple threads/processes may read and
   write shared state (order book snapshots, inventory, open orders)
   concurrently. Because exchanges process messages sequentially but
   your local system may process market data and order acknowledgments
   asynchronously, naive shared-state access WILL cause race conditions.

    def forecast_demand(self, historical_data, periods_ahead=12, alpha=0.3, beta=0.1):
        """
        Forecast demand per SKU using Holt's double exponential smoothing
        (level + trend), with fallback to moving average for sparse data.

        historical_data: dict {sku: [demand_values_in_chronological_order]}
        Returns: dict {sku: {'forecast': [...], 'level': x, 'trend': y, 'mape': z}}
        """
        forecasts = {}

        for sku, series in historical_data.items():
            series = [max(0.0, float(v)) for v in series]

            if len(series) < 2:
                avg = series[0] if series else 0.0
                forecasts[sku] = {
                    'forecast': [avg] * periods_ahead,
                    'level': avg,
                    'trend': 0.0,
                    'mape': None
                }
                continue

            # Initialize level and trend
            level = series[0]
            trend = series[1] - series[0]

            fitted = [level + trend]
            errors = []

            for t in range(1, len(series)):
                actual = series[t]
                prev_level = level
                level = alpha * actual + (1 - alpha) * (prev_level + trend)
                trend = beta * (level - prev_level) + (1 - beta) * trend
                fitted.append(level + trend)

            # Compute MAPE on fitted vs actual (skip first point)
            errs = []
            for t in range(1, len(series)):
                actual = series[t]
                pred = fitted[t - 1]
                if actual != 0:
                    errs.append(abs(actual - pred) / actual)
            mape = (sum(errs) / len(errs) * 100) if errs else None

            forecast_vals = []
            for h in range(1, periods_ahead + 1):
                forecast_vals.append(max(0.0, level + h * trend))

            forecasts[sku] = {
                'forecast': forecast_vals,
                'level': level,
                'trend': trend,
                'mape': mape

                'tier': tier,
                'risk_flags': risk_flags,
                'lead_time_days': lead_time
            }

        ranked = sorted(scorecards.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1]['composite_score'], reverse=True)
        self.supplier_scorecards = {
            'scorecards': scorecards,
            'ranking': [s[0] for s in ranked]
        }
        return self.supplier_scorecards

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 6. SHIPMENT TRACKING
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def track_shipments(self, shipments):
        """
        Track shipment statuses, flag delays, and compute delivery
        performance metrics.

        shipments: list of dicts, each with:
            {'id', 'origin', 'destination', 'ship_date' (datetime),
             'expected_arrival' (datetime), 'actual_arrival' (datetime or None),
             'status' (optional), 'current_location' (optional)}
        """
        now = datetime.now()
        tracked = {}
        delayed_count = 0
        in_transit_count = 0
        delivered_count = 0
        total_transit_days = []
        delay_days_list = []

        for shp in shipments:
            shp_id = shp.get('id')
            ship_date = shp.get('ship_date')
            expected = shp.get('expected_arrival')
            actual = shp.get('actual_arrival')

            if actual is not None:
                status = 'Delivered'
                delivered_count += 1
                if expected and actual > expected:
                    delay_days = (actual - expected).days
                    delay_days_list.append(delay_days)
                    status = 'Delivered Late'
                if ship_date:
                    total_transit_days.append((actual - ship_date).days)
            else:
                if expected and now > expected:
                    status = 'Delayed'
                    delayed_count += 1
                    delay_days_list.append((now - expected).days)
                else:
                    status = 'In Transit'
                    in_transit_count += 1

            tracked[shp_id] = {
                'origin': shp.get('origin'),
                'destination': shp.get('destination'),
                'ship_date': ship_date,
                'expected_arrival': expected,
                'actual_arrival': actual,
                'status': status,
                'current_location': shp.get('current_location', 'Unknown')
            }

        total_shipments = len(shipments)
        on_time_delivered = delivered_count - sum(
            1 for v in tracked.values() if v['status'] == 'Delivered Late'
        )
        on_time_rate = (on_time_delivered / delivered_count * 100) if delivered_count else None

        summary = {
            'total_shipments': total_shipments,
            'delivered': delivered_count,
            'in_transit': in_transit_count,
            'delayed': delayed_count,
            'on_time_delivery_rate_pct': round(on_time_rate, 2) if on_time_rate is not None else None,
            'avg_transit_days': round(statistics.mean(total_transit_days), 2) if total_transit_days else None,
            'avg_delay_days': round(statistics.mean(delay_days_list), 2) if delay_days_list else 0
        }

        self.shipment_tracker = {
            'shipments': tracked,
            'summary': summary
        }
        return self.shipment_tracker

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 7. PERFORMANCE DASHBOARD
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def generate_dashboard(self):
        """
        Aggregate all module outputs into a unified performance dashboard
        with KPIs and alerts.
        """
        dashboard = {
            'generated_at': datetime.now().isoformat(),
            'kpis': {},
            'alerts': [],
            'summary': {}
        }

        # Demand forecasting KPIs
        if self.demand_forecasts:
            mapes = [v['mape'] for v in self.demand_forecasts.values() if v['mape'] is not None]
            dashboard['kpis']['avg_forecast_mape_pct'] = round(statistics.mean(mapes), 2) if mapes else None
            dashboard['kpis']['skus_forecasted'] = len(self.demand_forecasts)

        # Inventory KPIs
        if self.inventory_plan:
            reorder_needed = [sku for sku, v in self.inventory_plan.items() if v['needs_reorder']]
            total_safety_stock = sum(v['safety_stock'] for v in self.inventory_plan.values())
            dashboard['kpis']['skus_needing_reorder'] = len(reorder_needed)
            dashboard['kpis']['total_safety_stock_units'] = round(total_safety_stock, 2)
            if reorder_needed:
                dashboard['alerts'].append(
                    f"{len(reorder_needed)} SKU(s) below reorder point: {reorder_needed[:10]}"
                )

        # Production KPIs
        if self.production_schedule:
            utilization = self.production_schedule.get('capacity_utilization_pct', [])
            if utilization:
                avg_util = round(statistics.mean(utilization), 2)
                dashboard['kpis']['avg_capacity_utilization_pct'] = avg_util
                if avg_util > 95:
                    dashboard['alerts'].append("Production capacity near saturation (>95% utilization)")
                elif avg_util < 40:
                    dashboard['alerts'].append("Production capacity underutilized (<40%)")

        # Logistics KPIs
        if self.logistics_plan:
            dashboard['kpis']['total_logistics_cost'] = self.logistics_plan.get('total_cost')
            unmet = self.logistics_plan.get('unmet_demand', {})
            if unmet:
                dashboard['alerts'].append(f"Unmet destination demand detected: {list(unmet.keys())}")

        # Supplier KPIs
        if self.supplier_scorecards:
            scorecards = self.supplier_scorecards.get('scorecards', {})
            at_risk = [s for s, v in scorecards.items() if v['tier'] == 'At Risk']
            avg_score = statistics.mean([v['composite_score'] for v in scorecards.values()]) if scorecards else None
            dashboard['kpis']['avg_supplier_score'] = round(avg_score, 2) if avg_score is not None else None
            dashboard['kpis']['at_risk_suppliers'] = len(at_risk)
            if at_risk:
                dashboard['alerts'].append(f"At-risk suppliers: {at_risk}")

        # Shipment KPIs
        if self.shipment_tracker:
            summary = self.shipment_tracker.get('summary', {})
            dashboard['kpis']['on_time_delivery_rate_pct'] = summary.get('on_time_delivery_rate_pct')
            dashboard['kpis']['delayed_shipments'] = summary.get('delayed')
            if summary.get('delayed', 0) > 0:
                dashboard['alerts'].append(f"{summary['delayed']} shipment(s) currently delayed")

        dashboard['summary'] = {
            'modules_active': [
                name for name, data in [
                    ('demand_forecasting', self.demand_forecasts),
                    ('inventory_optimization', self.inventory_plan),
                    ('production_planning', self.production_schedule),
                    ('logistics', self.logistics_plan),
                    ('supplier_management', self.supplier_scorecards),
                    ('shipment_tracking', self.shipment_tracker),
                ] if data
            ],
            'total_alerts': len(dashboard['alerts'])
        }

        self.dashboard = dashboard
        return dashboard


def optimize_supply_chain(historical_demand, lead_times, unit_costs,
                           capacity_per_period, warehouses, destinations,
                           shipping_costs, supplier_data, shipments,
                           order_costs=None, current_stock=None,
                           forecast_periods=12, production_rate=None,
                           shipment_volumes=None):
    """
    End-to-end supply chain optimization pipeline.

    Returns a dict containing forecasts, inventory plan, production schedule,
    logistics plan, supplier scorecards, shipment tracking, and a
    consolidated performance dashboard.
    """
    optimizer = SupplyChainOptimizer()

    forecasts = optimizer.forecast_demand(historical_demand, periods_ahead=forecast_periods)

    inventory_plan = optimizer.optimize_inventory(
        historical_demand, lead_times, unit_costs,
        order_costs=order_costs, current_stock=current_stock
    )

    production_schedule = optimizer.plan_production(
        capacity_per_period, periods=forecast_periods, production_rate=production_rate
    )

    logistics_plan = optimizer.coordinate_logistics(
        warehouses, destinations, shipping_costs, shipment_volumes=shipment_volumes
    )

    supplier_scorecards = optimizer.manage_suppliers(supplier_data)

    shipment_status = optimizer.track_shipments(shipments)

    dashboard = optimizer.generate_dashboard()

    return {
        'demand_forecasts': forecasts,
        'inventory_plan': inventory_plan,
        'production_schedule': production_schedule,
        'logistics_plan': logistics_plan,
        'supplier_scorecards': supplier_scorecards,
        'shipment_tracking': shipment_status,
        'dashboard': dashboard
    }

"""
Business Analytics Charting Module
===================================
A wrapper around matplotlib/seaborn providing branded business chart
templates, automated annotations, and consistent styling.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import io
import os
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any, Callable, Iterable, Optional, Sequence, Union

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker
from matplotlib.figure import Figure
from matplotlib.axes import Axes
from matplotlib.offsetbox import OffsetImage, AnnotationBbox
import matplotlib.image as mpimg
import seaborn as sns


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Branding / Theme
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

@dataclass
class BrandTheme:
    """Holds branding configuration: colors, fonts, logo, watermark."""

    name: str = "Default"
    primary_color: str = "#1F4E79"
    secondary_color: str = "#F2A900"
    palette: Sequence[str] = field(
        default_factory=lambda: [
            "#1F4E79", "#F2A900", "#5BA3D0", "#8AC926",
            "#C1121F", "#6A4C93", "#4D908E", "#9C6644",
        ]
    )
    background_color: str = "#FFFFFF"
    text_color: str = "#222222"
    grid_color: str = "#DDDDDD"
    font_family: str = "DejaVu Sans"
    title_font_size: int = 16
    subtitle_font_size: int = 11
    label_font_size: int = 10
    annotation_font_size: int = 9
    source_font_size: int = 8
    logo_path: Optional[str] = None
    logo_zoom: float = 0.08
    logo_position: str = "lower right"  # lower right, lower left, upper right, upper left
    watermark_text: Optional[str] = None
    company_name: str = "Your Company"

    def apply(self) -> None:
        """Apply this theme globally to matplotlib/seaborn rcParams."""
        sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")
        plt.rcParams.update({
            "figure.facecolor": self.background_color,
            "axes.facecolor": self.background_color,
            "axes.edgecolor": self.grid_color,
            "axes.labelcolor": self.text_color,
            "axes.grid": True,
            "grid.color": self.grid_color,
            "grid.linewidth": 0.6,
            "text.color": self.text_color,
            "xtick.color": self.text_color,
            "ytick.color": self.text_color,
            "font.family": self.font_family,
            "axes.titlesize": self.title_font_size,
            "axes.labelsize": self.label_font_size,
            "legend.fontsize": self.label_font_size,
            "figure.titlesize": self.title_font_size,
            "axes.spines.top": False,
            "axes.spines.right": False,
        })
        sns.set_palette(self.palette)


DEFAULT_THEME = BrandTheme()


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Utility helpers
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _human_format(num: float, precision: int = 1) -> str:
    """Format large numbers as 1.2K, 3.4M, etc."""
    if num is None or (isinstance(num, float) and np.isnan(num)):
        return "N/A"
    magnitude = 0
    abs_num = abs(num)
    suffixes = ["", "K", "M", "B", "T"]
    while abs_num >= 1000 and magnitude < len(suffixes) - 1:
        abs_num /= 1000.0
        magnitude += 1
    sign = "-" if num < 0 else ""
    return f"{sign}{abs_num:.{precision}f}{suffixes[magnitude]}"


def _percent_format(x: float, decimals: int = 1) -> str:
    return f"{x * 100:.{decimals}f}%"


def _pct_change(old: float, new: float) -> Optional[float]:
    if old in (0, None) or old != old:  # NaN check
        return None
    return (new - old) / abs(old)


def _add_source_note(ax: Axes, theme: BrandTheme, source: Optional[str],
                      generated_note: bool = True) -> None:
    text_parts = []
    if source:
        text_parts.append(f"Source: {source}")
    if generated_note:
        text_parts.append(f"{theme.company_name} Analytics")
    if not text_parts:
        return
    fig = ax.get_figure()
    fig.text(
        0.01, 0.01, "  |  ".join(text_parts),
        fontsize=theme.source_font_size, color=theme.text_color,
        alpha=0.6, ha="left", va="bottom"
    )


def _add_logo(fig: Figure, theme: BrandTheme) -> None:
    if not theme.logo_path or not os.path.exists(theme.logo_path):
        return
    try:
        img = mpimg.imread(theme.logo_path)
    except Exception:
        return
    imagebox = OffsetImage(img, zoom=theme.logo_zoom)
    positions = {
        "lower right": (0.98, 0.02, "right", "bottom"),
        "lower left": (0.02, 0.02, "left", "bottom"),
        "upper right": (0.98, 0.97, "right", "top"),
        "upper left": (0.02, 0.97, "left", "top"),
    }
    x, y, ha, va = positions.get(theme.logo_position, positions["lower right"])
    ab = AnnotationBbox(
        imagebox, (x, y), xycoords="figure fraction",
        frameon=False, box_alignment=(1 if ha == "right" else 0,
                                       1 if va == "top" else 0)
    )
    fig.add_artist(ab)


def _add_watermark(fig: Figure, theme: BrandTheme) -> None:
    if not theme.watermark_text:
        return
    fig.text(
        0.5, 0.5, theme.watermark_text,
        fontsize=40, color=theme.text_color, alpha=0.06,
        ha="center", va="center", rotation=30, zorder=0
    )


def _title_block(fig: Figure, ax: Axes, theme: BrandTheme,
                  title: str, subtitle: Optional[str] = None) -> None:
    ax.set_title("")
    fig.suptitle(
        title, x=0.06, ha="left", fontsize=theme.title_font_size,
        fontweight="bold", color=theme.text_color, y=0.98
    )
    if subtitle:
        fig.text(
            0.06, 0.925, subtitle, ha="left",
            fontsize=theme.subtitle_font_size, color=theme.text_color, alpha=0.75
        )


def _finalize(fig: Figure, ax: Axes, theme: BrandTheme, source: Optional[str]) -> None:
    _add_logo(fig, theme)
    _add_watermark(fig, theme)
    _add_source_note(ax, theme, source)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Automated annotation helpers
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def annotate_extremes(ax: Axes, x: Sequence, y: Sequence, theme: BrandTheme,
                       fmt: Callable[[float], str] = _human_format) -> None:
    """Annotate max and min points on a line/scatter chart."""
    if len(y) == 0:
        return
    y_arr = np.asarray(y, dtype=float)
    if np.all(np.isnan(y_arr)):
        return
    max_idx = int(np.nanargmax(y_arr))
    min_idx = int(np.nanargmin(y_arr))
    for idx, label, color in [
        (max_idx, "Peak", theme.secondary_color),
        (min_idx, "Low", theme.primary_color),
    ]:
        if idx == max_idx and idx == min_idx and label == "Low":
            continue
        ax.annotate(
            f"{label}: {fmt(y_arr[idx])}",
            xy=(x[idx], y_arr[idx]),
            xytext=(0, 12 if label == "Peak" else -18),
            textcoords="offset points",
            ha="center",
            fontsize=theme.annotation_font_size,
            color=color,
            fontweight="bold",
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-", color=color, lw=0.8, alpha=0.7),
        )


def annotate_last_value(ax: Axes, x: Sequence, y: Sequence, theme: BrandTheme,
                         fmt: Callable[[float], str] = _human_format,
                         label_prefix: str = "") -> None:
    """Highlight and label the last data point (common in trend charts)."""
    if len(y) == 0:
        return
    last_x, last_y = x[-1], y[-1]
    ax.scatter([last_x], [last_y], color=theme.secondary_color, zorder=5, s=40)
    ax.annotate(
        f"{label_prefix}{fmt(last_y)}",
        xy=(last_x, last_y),
        xytext=(8, 0),
        textcoords="offset points",
        va="center",
        fontsize=theme.annotation_font_size,
        fontweight="bold",
        color=theme.secondary_color,
    )


def annotate_growth(ax: Axes, x: Sequence, y: Sequence, theme: BrandTheme) -> None:
    """Add a growth-rate callout comparing first and last values."""
    if len(y) < 2:
        return
    change = _pct_change(y[0], y[-1])
    if change is None:
        return
    color = theme.secondary_color if change >= 0 else "#C1121F"
    arrow = "▲" if change >= 0 else "▼"
    ax.text(
        0.99, 0.95, f"{arrow} {_percent_format(abs(change))} overall",
        transform=ax.transAxes, ha="right", va="top",
        fontsize=theme.annotation_font_size + 1, fontweight="bold", color=color,
        bbox=dict(boxstyle="round,pad=0.3", fc="white", ec=color, alpha=0.85),
    )


def annotate_target_line(ax: Axes, target: float, theme: BrandTheme,
                          label: str = "Target",
                          fmt: Callable[[float], str] = _human_format) -> None:
    """Draw a horizontal target/goal reference line with label."""
    ax.axhline(target, color=theme.primary_color, linestyle="--", linewidth=1.2, alpha=0.8)
    ax.text(
        1.0, target, f" {label}: {fmt(target)}",
        transform=ax.get_yaxis_transform(), va="center", ha="left",
        fontsize=theme.annotation_font_size, color=theme.primary_color,
        fontweight="bold",
    )


def annotate_bar_values(ax: Axes, fmt: Callable[[float], str] = _human_format,
                         orientation: str = "vertical") -> None:
    """Add value labels above/beside each bar in a bar chart."""
    for patch in ax.patches:
        if orientation == "vertical":
            height = patch.get_height()
            if np.isnan(height):
                continue
            x = patch.get_x() + patch.get_width() / 2
            ax.annotate(
                fmt(height), (x, height),
                ha="center", va="bottom",
                fontsize=8, xytext=(0, 3), textcoords="offset points",
            )
        else:
            width = patch.get_width()
            if np.isnan(width):
                continue
            y = patch.get_y() + patch.get_height() / 2
            ax.annotate(
                fmt(width), (width, y),
                ha="left", va="center",
                fontsize=8, xytext=(3, 0), textcoords="offset points",
            )


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Main API: BusinessChart class
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

class BusinessChart:
    """
    High-level chart builder wrapping matplotlib/seaborn with business
    templates, branding, and automatic annotations.

    Example:
        bc = BusinessChart(theme=my_theme)
        fig = bc.kpi_trend(df, x="month", y="revenue", title="Monthly Revenue")
        bc.save(fig, "revenue.png")
    """

    def __init__(self, theme: Optional[BrandTheme] = None, figsize: tuple = (10, 6),
                 dpi: int = 120):
        self.theme = theme or DEFAULT_THEME
        self.figsize = figsize
        self.dpi = dpi
        self.theme.apply()

    # -- internal helper -----------------------------------------------

    def _new_fig(self) -> tuple[Figure, Axes]:
        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=self.figsize, dpi=self.dpi)
        fig.patch.set_facecolor(self.theme.background_color)
        fig.subplots_adjust(top=0.85, bottom=0.15)
        return fig, ax

    def _y_axis_currency(self, ax: Axes, currency: str = "$") -> None:
        ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(
            mticker.FuncFormatter(lambda v, _: f"{currency}{_human_format(v)}")
        )

    def _y_axis_percent(self, ax: Axes) -> None:
        ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(
            mticker.FuncFormatter(lambda v, _: f"{v * 100:.0f}%")
        )

    # -- Templates -------------------------------------------------------

    def kpi_trend(
        self, df: pd.DataFrame, x: str, y: str,
        title: str = "KPI Trend", subtitle: Optional[str] = None,
        target: Optional[float] = None, currency: Optional[str] = None,
        percent: bool = False, source: Optional[str] = None,
        annotate: bool = True,
    ) -> Figure:
        """Line chart for tracking a KPI over time with auto annotations."""
        fig, ax = self._new_fig()
        data = df.sort_values(x)
        x_vals = data[x].tolist()
        y_vals = data[y].tolist()

        ax.plot(x_vals, y_vals, color=self.theme.primary_color, linewidth=2.5,
                marker="o", markersize=4)
        ax.fill_between(range(len(x_vals)), y_vals, alpha=0.08,
                         color=self.theme.primary_color)

        if currency:
            self._y_axis_currency(ax, currency)
        elif percent:
            self._y_axis_percent(ax)
        else:
            ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(
                mticker.FuncFormatter(lambda v, _: _human_format(v))
            )

        ax.set_xlabel("")
        ax.set_ylabel(y)
        plt.setp(ax.get_xticklabels(), rotation=30, ha="right")

        fmt = (lambda v: f"{currency}{_human_format(v)}") if currency else \
              (_percent_format if percent else _human_format)

        if annotate:
            annotate_extremes(ax, x_vals, y_vals, self.theme, fmt=fmt)
            annotate_last_value(ax, x_vals, y_vals, self.theme, fmt=fmt)
            annotate_growth(ax, x_vals, y_vals, self.theme)
        if target is not None:
            annotate_target_line(ax, target, self.theme, fmt=fmt)

        _title_block(fig, ax, self.theme, title, subtitle)
        _finalize(fig, ax, self.theme, source)
        return fig

    def category_comparison(
        self, df: pd.DataFrame, category: str, value: str,
        title: str = "Category Comparison", subtitle: Optional[str] = None,
        horizontal: bool = True, currency: Optional[str] = None,
        top_n: Optional[int] = None, highlight_top: bool = True,
        source: Optional[str] = None,
    ) -> Figure:
        """Bar chart comparing categories, sorted, with value labels."""
        fig, ax = self._new_fig()
        data = df[[category, value]].dropna().sort_values(value, ascending=horizontal)
        if top_n:
            data = data.tail(top_n) if horizontal else data.head(top_n)

        colors = [self.theme.primary_color] * len(data)
        if highlight_top and len(data) > 0:
            top_idx = data[value].values.argmax()
            colors[top_idx] = self.theme.secondary_color

        fmt = (lambda v: f"{currency}{_human_format(v)}") if currency else _human_format

        if horizontal:
            ax.barh(data[category], data[value], color=colors)
            self._y_axis_currency(ax, currency) if False else None
            ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(
                mticker.FuncFormatter(lambda v, _: fmt(v))
            )
            annotate_bar_values(ax, fmt=fmt, orientation="horizontal")
        else:
            ax.bar(data[category], data[value], color=colors)
            ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(
                mticker.FuncFormatter(lambda v, _: fmt(v))
            )
            plt.setp(ax.get_xticklabels(), rotation=30, ha="right")
            annotate_bar_values(ax, fmt=fmt, orientation="vertical")

        ax.set_xlabel("")
        ax.set_ylabel("")

        _title_block(fig, ax, self.theme, title, subtitle)
        _finalize(fig, ax, self.theme, source)
        return fig

    def part_to_whole(
        self, df: pd.DataFrame, category: str, value: str,
        title: str = "Composition Breakdown", subtitle: Optional[str] = None,
        donut: bool = True, source: Optional[str] = None,
        min_pct_label: float = 0.03,
    ) -> Figure:
        """Pie/donut chart with percentage annotations, small slices grouped as 'Other'."""
        fig, ax = self._new_fig()
        data = df[[category, value]].dropna().sort_values(value, ascending=False)
        total = data[value].sum()
        data["_pct"] = data[value] / total

        small = data[data["_pct"] < min_pct_label]
        big = data[data["_pct"] >= min_pct_label]
        if len(small) > 1:
            other_row = pd.DataFrame({
                category: ["Other"],
                value: [small[value].sum()],
                "_pct": [small["_pct"].sum()],
            })
            plot_data = pd.concat([big, other_row], ignore_index=True)
        else:
            plot_data = data

        colors = (self.theme.palette * (len(plot_data) // len(self.theme.palette) + 1))[:len(plot_data)]
        wedgeprops = dict(width=0.4) if donut else {}

        wedges, _texts, autotexts = ax.pie(
            plot_data[value],
            labels=plot_data[category],
            autopct=lambda p: f"{p:.1f}%" if p >= min_pct_label * 100 else "",
            colors=colors,
            wedgeprops=wedgeprops,
            pctdistance=0.8 if donut else 0.6,
            startangle=90,
            textprops={"fontsize": self.theme.label_font_size},
        )
        for at in autotexts:
            at.set_color("white")
            at.set_fontweight("bold")
            at.set_fontsize(self.theme.annotation_font_size)

        if donut:
            ax.text(0, 0, f"Total\n{_human_format(total)}", ha="center", va="center",
                    fontsize=self.theme.label_font_size + 1, fontweight="bold",
                    color=self.theme.text_color)

        ax.set_ylabel("")
        _title_block(fig, ax, self.theme, title, subtitle)
        _finalize(fig, ax, self.theme, source)
        return fig

    def variance_waterfall(
        self, labels: Sequence[str], values: Sequence[float],
        title: str = "Variance Bridge", subtitle: Optional[str] = None,
        currency: Optional[str] = None, source: Optional[str] = None,
        total_label: str = "Total",
    ) -> Figure:
        """Waterfall chart showing sequential contributions to a total."""
        fig, ax = self._new_fig()
        n = len(values)
        cumulative = np.cumsum(values)
        starts = np.concatenate(([0], cumulative[:-1]))

        colors = []
        for v in values:
            if v >= 0:
                colors.append(self.theme.secondary_color)
            else:
                colors.append("#C1121F")
        colors[-1] = self.theme.primary_color  # total bar assumed last

        fmt = (lambda v: f"{currency}{_human_format(v)}") if currency else _human_format

        for i in range(n):
            base = 0 if i == n - 1 else starts[i]
            height = values[i] if i != n - 1 else cumulative[-2] if n > 1 else values[i]
            if i == n - 1:
                ax.bar(i, values[i], bottom=0, color=colors[i])
                label_y = values[i]
            else:
                ax.bar(i, values[i], bottom=starts[i], color=colors[i])
                label_y = starts[i] + values[i]
            ax.annotate(
                fmt(values[i]), (i, label_y),
                ha="center", va="bottom" if values[i] >= 0 else "top",
                fontsize=self.theme.annotation_font_size, xytext=(0, 3),
                textcoords="offset points",
            )
            if i < n - 1:
                ax.plot([i, i + 1], [cumulative[i], cumulative[i]],
                        color="gray", linewidth=0.8, linestyle=":")

        ax.set_xticks(range(n))
        ax.set_xticklabels(labels, rotation=30, ha="right")
        ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(mticker.FuncFormatter(lambda v, _: fmt(v)))
        ax.set_xlabel("")

        _title_block(fig, ax, self.theme, title, subtitle)
        _finalize(fig, ax, self.theme, source)
        return fig

    def cohort_heatmap(
        self, df: pd.DataFrame, index: str, columns: str, values: str,
        title: str = "Cohort Analysis", subtitle: Optional[str] = None,
        fmt: str = ".0%", cmap: Optional[str] = None, source: Optional[str] = None,
    ) -> Figure:
        """Heatmap for cohort/retention style analysis."""
        pivot = df.pivot(index=index, columns=columns, values=values)
        fig, ax = self._new_fig()
        cmap = cmap or sns.light_palette(self.theme.primary_color, as_cmap=True)
        sns.heatmap(
            pivot, annot=True, fmt=fmt, cmap=cmap, ax=ax,
            linewidths=0.5, linecolor=self.theme.background_color,
            cbar_kws={"shrink": 0.7},
            annot_kws={"fontsize": self.theme.annotation_font_size},
        )
        ax.set_xlabel(columns)
        ax.set_ylabel(index)

        _title_block(fig, ax, self.theme, title, subtitle)
        _finalize(fig, ax, self.theme, source)
        return fig

    def correlation_scatter(
        self, df: pd.DataFrame, x: str, y: str, hue: Optional[str] = None,
        title: str = "Relationship Analysis", subtitle: Optional[str] = None,
        show_trendline: bool = True, source: Optional[str] = None,
    ) -> Figure:
        """Scatter plot with optional trendline and correlation annotation."""
        fig, ax = self._new_fig()
        sns.scatterplot(
            data=df, x=x, y=y, hue=hue, ax=ax,
            palette=self.theme.palette if hue else None,
            color=None if hue else self.theme.primary_color,
            s=50, alpha=0.75, edgecolor="white", linewidth=0.5,
        )

        if show_trendline:
            clean = df[[x, y]].dropna()
            if len(clean) > 1:
                z = np.polyfit(clean[x], clean[y], 1)
                p = np.poly1d(z)
                x_line = np.linspace(clean[x].min(), clean[x].max(), 100)
                ax.plot(x_line, p(x_line), color=self.theme.secondary_color,
                        linestyle="--", linewidth=2)
                corr = clean[x].corr(clean[y])
                ax.text(
                    0.02, 0.95, f"r = {corr:.2f}", transform=ax.transAxes,
                    fontsize=self.theme.annotation_font_size + 1, fontweight="bold",
                    color=self.theme.secondary_color,
                    bbox=dict(boxstyle="round,pad=0.3", fc="white",
                              ec=self.theme.secondary_color, alpha=0.85),
                )

        _title_block(fig, ax, self.theme, title, subtitle)
        _finalize(fig, ax, self.theme, source)
        return fig

    def distribution(
        self, df: pd.DataFrame, value: str, group: Optional[str] = None,
        title: str = "Distribution", subtitle: Optional[str] = None,
        kind: str = "hist", source: Optional[str] = None,
    ) -> Figure:
        """Histogram/box/violin distribution chart with mean/median annotations."""
        fig, ax = self._new_fig()

        if kind == "hist":
            if group:
                for i, (name, sub) in enumerate(df.groupby(group)):
                    color = self.theme.palette[i % len(self.theme.palette)]
                    sns.histplot(sub[value], ax=ax, color=color, label=str(name),
                                 kde=True, alpha=0.5, stat="density")
                ax.legend(title=group)
            else:
                sns.histplot(df[value], ax=ax, color=self.theme.primary_color,
                             kde=True, alpha=0.6)
                mean_v = df[value].mean()
                median_v = df[value].median()
                ax.axvline(mean_v, color=self.theme.secondary_color, linestyle="--",
                           label=f"Mean: {_human_format(mean_v)}")
                ax.axvline(median_v, color="#C1121F", linestyle=":",
                           label=f"Median: {_human_format(median_v)}")
                ax.legend()
        elif kind == "box":
            sns.boxplot(data=df, x=group, y=value, ax=ax,
                        palette=self.theme.palette if group else None,
                        color=None if group else self.theme.primary_color)
        elif kind == "violin":
            sns.violinplot(data=df, x=group, y=value, ax=ax,
                           palette=self.theme.palette if group else None,
                           color=None if group else self.theme.primary_color)
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"Unsupported kind: {kind}")

        _title_block(fig, ax, self.theme, title, subtitle)
        _finalize(fig, ax, self.theme, source)
        return fig

    def multi_series_trend(
        self, df: pd.DataFrame, x: str, y: str, series: str,
        title: str = "Trend Comparison", subtitle: Optional[str] = None,
        currency: Optional[str] = None, percent: bool = False,
        source: Optional[str] = None, annotate_last: bool = True,
    ) -> Figure:
        """Multi-line trend chart comparing several series."""
        fig, ax = self._new_fig()
        fmt = (lambda v: f"{currency}{_human_format(v)}") if currency else \
              (_percent_format if percent else _human_format)

        for i, (name, sub) in enumerate(df.groupby(series)):
            sub = sub.sort_values(x)
            color = self.theme.palette[i % len(self.theme.palette)]
            ax.plot(sub[x], sub[y], marker="o", markersize=3, linewidth=2,
                    color=color, label=str(name))
            if annotate_last:
                annotate_last_value(ax, sub[x].tolist(), sub[y].tolist(),
                                     BrandTheme(**{**self.theme.__dict__,
                                                   "secondary_color": color}),
                                     fmt=fmt, label_prefix=f"{name}: ")

        if currency:
            self._y_axis_currency(ax, currency)
        elif percent:
            self._y_axis_percent(ax)

        ax.legend(loc="upper left", frameon=False)
        plt.setp(ax.get_xticklabels(), rotation=30, ha="right")

        _title_block(fig, ax, self.theme, title, subtitle)
        _finalize(fig, ax, self.theme, source)
        return fig

    # -- Output ----------------------------------------------------------

    def save(self, fig: Figure, path: str, transparent: bool = False) -> str:
        fig.savefig(path, dpi=self.dpi, bbox_inches="tight",
                    facecolor=fig.get_facecolor(), transparent=transparent)
        return path

    def to_bytes(self, fig: Figure, fmt: str = "png") -> bytes:
        buf = io.BytesIO()
        fig.savefig(buf, format=fmt, dpi=self.dpi, bbox_inches="tight",
                    facecolor=fig.get_facecolor())
        buf.seek(0)
        return buf.getvalue()

    @staticmethod
    def show(fig: Figure) -> None:
        plt.show()

    @staticmethod
    def close(fig: Figure) -> None:
        plt.close(fig)

"""
Business Analytics Charting Module
===================================
A wrapper around matplotlib/seaborn providing branded business chart
templates, automated annotations, and consistent styling.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import io
import os
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any, Callable, Iterable, Optional, Sequence, Union

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker
from matplotlib.figure import Figure
from matplotlib.axes import Axes
from matplotlib.offsetbox import OffsetImage, AnnotationBbox
import matplotlib.image as mpimg
import seaborn as sns


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Branding / Theme
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

@dataclass
class BrandTheme:
    """Holds branding configuration: colors, fonts, logo, watermark."""

    name: str = "Default"
    primary_color: str = "#1F4E79"
    secondary_color: str = "#F2A900"
    palette: Sequence[str] = field(
        default_factory=lambda: [
            "#1F4E79", "#F2A900", "#5BA3D0", "#8AC926",
            "#C1121F", "#6A4C93", "#4D908E", "#9C6644",
        ]
    )
    background_color: str = "#FFFFFF"
    text_color: str = "#222222"
    grid_color: str = "#DDDDDD"
    font_family: str = "DejaVu Sans"
    title_font_size: int = 16
    subtitle_font_size: int = 11
    label_font_size: int = 10
    annotation_font_size: int = 9
    source_font_size: int = 8
    logo_path: Optional[str] = None
    logo_zoom: float = 0.08
    logo_position: str = "lower right"  # lower right, lower left, upper right, upper left
    watermark_text: Optional[str] = None
    company_name: str = "Your Company"

    def apply(self) -> None:
        """Apply this theme globally to matplotlib/seaborn rcParams."""
        sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")
        plt.rcParams.update({
            "figure.facecolor": self.background_color,
            "axes.facecolor": self.background_color,
            "axes.edgecolor": self.grid_color,
            "axes.labelcolor": self.text_color,
            "axes.grid": True,
            "grid.color": self.grid_color,
            "grid.linewidth": 0.6,
            "text.color": self.text_color,
            "xtick.color": self.text_color,
            "ytick.color": self.text_color,
            "font.family": self.font_family,
            "axes.titlesize": self.title_font_size,
            "axes.labelsize": self.label_font_size,
            "legend.fontsize": self.label_font_size,
            "figure.titlesize": self.title_font_size,
            "axes.spines.top": False,
            "axes.spines.right": False,
        })
        sns.set_palette(self.palette)


DEFAULT_THEME = BrandTheme()


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Utility helpers
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _human_format(num: float, precision: int = 1) -> str:
    """Format large numbers as 1.2K, 3.4M, etc."""
    if num is None or (isinstance(num, float) and np.isnan(num)):
        return "N/A"
    magnitude = 0
    abs_num = abs(num)
    suffixes = ["", "K", "M", "B", "T"]
    while abs_num >= 1000 and magnitude < len(suffixes) - 1:
        abs_num /= 1000.0
        magnitude += 1
    sign = "-" if num < 0 else ""
    return f"{sign}{abs_num:.{precision}f}{suffixes[magnitude]}"


def _percent_format(x: float, decimals: int = 1) -> str:
    return f"{x * 100:.{decimals}f}%"


def _pct_change(old: float, new: float) -> Optional[float]:
    if old in (0, None) or old != old:  # NaN check
        return None
    return (new - old) / abs(old)


def _add_source_note(ax: Axes, theme: BrandTheme, source: Optional[str],
                      generated_note: bool = True) -> None:
    text_parts = []
    if source:
        text_parts.append(f"Source: {source}")
    if generated_note:
        text_parts.append(f"{theme.company_name} Analytics")
    if not text_parts:
        return
    fig = ax.get_figure()
    fig.text(
        0.01, 0.01, "  |  ".join(text_parts),
        fontsize=theme.source_font_size, color=theme.text_color,
        alpha=0.6, ha="left", va="bottom"
    )


def _add_logo(fig: Figure, theme: BrandTheme) -> None:
    if not theme.logo_path or not os.path.exists(theme.logo_path):
        return
    try:
        img = mpimg.imread(theme.logo_path)
    except Exception:
        return
    imagebox = OffsetImage(img, zoom=theme.logo_zoom)
    positions = {
        "lower right": (0.98, 0.02, "right", "bottom"),
        "lower left": (0.02, 0.02, "left", "bottom"),
        "upper right": (0.98, 0.97, "right", "top"),
        "upper left": (0.02, 0.97, "left", "top"),
    }
    x, y, ha, va = positions.get(theme.logo_position, positions["lower right"])
    ab = AnnotationBbox(
        imagebox, (x, y), xycoords="figure fraction",
        frameon=False, box_alignment=(1 if ha == "right" else 0,
                                       1 if va == "top" else 0)
    )
    fig.add_artist(ab)


def _add_watermark(fig: Figure, theme: BrandTheme) -> None:
    if not theme.watermark_text:
        return
    fig.text(
        0.5, 0.5, theme.watermark_text,
        fontsize=40, color=theme.text_color, alpha=0.06,
        ha="center", va="center", rotation=30, zorder=0
    )


def _title_block(fig: Figure, ax: Axes, theme: BrandTheme,
                  title: str, subtitle: Optional[str] = None) -> None:
    ax.set_title("")
    fig.suptitle(
        title, x=0.06, ha="left", fontsize=theme.title_font_size,
        fontweight="bold", color=theme.text_color, y=0.98
    )
    if subtitle:
        fig.text(
            0.06, 0.925, subtitle, ha="left",
            fontsize=theme.subtitle_font_size, color=theme.text_color, alpha=0.75
        )


def _finalize(fig: Figure, ax: Axes, theme: BrandTheme, source: Optional[str]) -> None:
    _add_logo(fig, theme)
    _add_watermark(fig, theme)
    _add_source_note(ax, theme, source)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Automated annotation helpers
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def annotate_extremes(ax: Axes, x: Sequence, y: Sequence, theme: BrandTheme,
                       fmt: Callable[[float], str] = _human_format) -> None:
    """Annotate max and min points on a line/scatter chart."""
    if len(y) == 0:
        return
    y_arr = np.asarray(y, dtype=float)
    if np.all(np.isnan(y_arr)):
        return
    max_idx = int(np.nanargmax(y_arr))
    min_idx = int(np.nanargmin(y_arr))
    for idx, label, color in [
        (max_idx, "Peak", theme.secondary_color),
        (min_idx, "Low", theme.primary_color),
    ]:
        if idx == max_idx and idx == min_idx and label == "Low":
            continue
        ax.annotate(
            f"{label}: {fmt(y_arr[idx])}",
            xy=(x[idx], y_arr[idx]),
            xytext=(0, 12 if label == "Peak" else -18),
            textcoords="offset points",
            ha="center",
            fontsize=theme.annotation_font_size,
            color=color,
            fontweight="bold",
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-", color=color, lw=0.8, alpha=0.7),
        )


def annotate_last_value(ax: Axes, x: Sequence, y: Sequence, theme: BrandTheme,
                         fmt: Callable[[float], str] = _human_format,
                         label_prefix: str = "") -> None:
    """Highlight and label the last data point (common in trend charts)."""
    if len(y) == 0:
        return
    last_x, last_y = x[-1], y[-1]
    ax.scatter([last_x], [last_y], color=theme.secondary_color, zorder=5, s=40)
    ax.annotate(
        f"{label_prefix}{fmt(last_y)}",
        xy=(last_x, last_y),
        xytext=(8, 0),
        textcoords="offset points",
        va="center",
        fontsize=theme.annotation_font_size,
        fontweight="bold",
        color=theme.secondary_color,
    )


def annotate_growth(ax: Axes, x: Sequence, y: Sequence, theme: BrandTheme) -> None:
    """Add a growth-rate callout comparing first and last values."""
    if len(y) < 2:
        return
    change = _pct_change(y[0], y[-1])
    if change is None:
        return
    color = theme.secondary_color if change >= 0 else "#C1121F"
    arrow = "▲" if change >= 0 else "▼"
    ax.text(
        0.99, 0.95, f"{arrow} {_percent_format(abs(change))} overall",
        transform=ax.transAxes, ha="right", va="top",
        fontsize=theme.annotation_font_size + 1, fontweight="bold", color=color,
        bbox=dict(boxstyle="round,pad=0.3", fc="white", ec=color, alpha=0.85),
    )


def annotate_target_line(ax: Axes, target: float, theme: BrandTheme,
                          label: str = "Target",
                          fmt: Callable[[float], str] = _human_format) -> None:
    """Draw a horizontal target/goal reference line with label."""
    ax.axhline(target, color=theme.primary_color, linestyle="--", linewidth=1.2, alpha=0.8)
    ax.text(
        1.0, target, f" {label}: {fmt(target)}",
        transform=ax.get_yaxis_transform(), va="center", ha="left",
        fontsize=theme.annotation_font_size, color=theme.primary_color,
        fontweight="bold",
    )


def annotate_bar_values(ax: Axes, fmt: Callable[[float], str] = _human_format,
                         orientation: str = "vertical") -> None:
    """Add value labels above/beside each bar in a bar chart."""
    for patch in ax.patches:
        if orientation == "vertical":
            height = patch.get_height()
            if np.isnan(height):
                continue
            x = patch.get_x() + patch.get_width() / 2
            ax.annotate(
                fmt(height), (x, height),
                ha="center", va="bottom",
                fontsize=8, xytext=(0, 3), textcoords="offset points",
            )
        else:
            width = patch.get_width()
            if np.isnan(width):
                continue
            y = patch.get_y() + patch.get_height() / 2
            ax.annotate(
                fmt(width), (width, y),
                ha="left", va="center",
                fontsize=8, xytext=(3, 0), textcoords="offset points",
            )


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Main API: BusinessChart class
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

class BusinessChart:
    """
    High-level chart builder wrapping matplotlib/seaborn with business
    templates, branding, and automatic annotations.

    Example:
        bc = BusinessChart(theme=my_theme)
        fig = bc.kpi_trend(df, x="month", y="revenue", title="Monthly Revenue")
        bc.save(fig, "revenue.png")
    """

    def __init__(self, theme: Optional[BrandTheme] = None, figsize: tuple = (10, 6),
                 dpi: int = 120):
        self.theme = theme or DEFAULT_THEME
        self.figsize = figsize
        self.dpi = dpi
        self.theme.apply()

    # -- internal helper -----------------------------------------------

    def _new_fig(self) -> tuple[Figure, Axes]:
        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=self.figsize, dpi=self.dpi)
        fig.patch.set_facecolor(self.theme.background_color)
        fig.subplots_adjust(top=0.85, bottom=0.15)
        return fig, ax

    def _y_axis_currency(self, ax: Axes, currency: str = "$") -> None:
        ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(
            mticker.FuncFormatter(lambda v, _: f"{currency}{_human_format(v)}")
        )

    def _y_axis_percent(self, ax: Axes) -> None:
        ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(
            mticker.FuncFormatter(lambda v, _: f"{v * 100:.0f}%")
        )

    # -- Templates -------------------------------------------------------

    def kpi_trend(
        self, df: pd.DataFrame, x: str, y: str,
        title: str = "KPI Trend", subtitle: Optional[str] = None,
        target: Optional[float] = None, currency: Optional[str] = None,
        percent: bool = False, source: Optional[str] = None,
        annotate: bool = True,
    ) -> Figure:
        """Line chart for tracking a KPI over time with auto annotations."""
        fig, ax = self._new_fig()
        data = df.sort_values(x)
        x_vals = data[x].tolist()
        y_vals = data[y].tolist()

        ax.plot(x_vals, y_vals, color=self.theme.primary_color, linewidth=2.5,
                marker="o", markersize=4)
        ax.fill_between(range(len(x_vals)), y_vals, alpha=0.08,
                         color=self.theme.primary_color)

        if currency:
            self._y_axis_currency(ax, currency)
        elif percent:
            self._y_axis_percent(ax)
        else:
            ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(
                mticker.FuncFormatter(lambda v, _: _human_format(v))
            )

        ax.set_xlabel("")
        ax.set_ylabel(y)
        plt.setp(ax.get_xticklabels(), rotation=30, ha="right")

        fmt = (lambda v: f"{currency}{_human_format(v)}") if currency else \
              (_percent_format if percent else _human_format)

        if annotate:
            annotate_extremes(ax, x_vals, y_vals, self.theme, fmt=fmt)
            annotate_last_value(ax, x_vals, y_vals, self.theme, fmt=fmt)
            annotate_growth(ax, x_vals, y_vals, self.theme)
        if target is not None:
            annotate_target_line(ax, target, self.theme, fmt=fmt)

        _title_block(fig, ax, self.theme, title, subtitle)
        _finalize(fig, ax, self.theme, source)
        return fig

    def category_comparison(
        self, df: pd.DataFrame, category: str, value: str,
        title: str = "Category Comparison", subtitle: Optional[str] = None,
        horizontal: bool = True, currency: Optional[str] = None,
        top_n: Optional[int] = None, highlight_top: bool = True,
        source: Optional[str] = None,
    ) -> Figure:
        """Bar chart comparing categories, sorted, with value labels."""
        fig, ax = self._new_fig()
        data = df[[category, value]].dropna().sort_values(value, ascending=horizontal)
        if top_n:
            data = data.tail(top_n) if horizontal else data.head(top_n)

        colors = [self.theme.primary_color] * len(data)
        if highlight_top and len(data) > 0:
            top_idx = data[value].values.argmax()
            colors[top_idx] = self.theme.secondary_color

        fmt = (lambda v: f"{currency}{_human_format(v)}") if currency else _human_format

        if horizontal:
            ax.barh(data[category], data[value], color=colors)
            self._y_axis_currency(ax, currency) if False else None
            ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(
                mticker.FuncFormatter(lambda v, _: fmt(v))
            )
            annotate_bar_values(ax, fmt=fmt, orientation="horizontal")
        else:
            ax.bar(data[category], data[value], color=colors)
            ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(
                mticker.FuncFormatter(lambda v, _: fmt(v))
            )

            annotate_bar_values(ax, fmt=fmt, orientation="vertical")

        ax.set_xlabel("")
        ax.set_ylabel("")

        _title_block(fig, ax, self.theme, title, subtitle)
        _finalize(fig, ax, self.theme, source)

    def part_to_whole(
        self, df: pd.DataFrame, category: str, value: str,
        title: str = "Composition Breakdown", subtitle: Optional[str] = None,
        donut: bool = True, source: Optional[str] = None,
        min_pct_label: float = 0.03,
    ) -> Figure:
        """Pie/donut chart with percentage annotations, small slices grouped as 'Other'."""
        fig, ax = self._new_fig()
        data = df[[category, value]].dropna().sort_values(value, ascending=False)
        total = data[value].sum()
        data["_pct"] = data[value] / total

        small = data[data["_pct"] < min_pct_label]
        big = data[data["_pct"] >= min_pct_label]
        if len(small) > 1:
            other_row = pd.DataFrame({
                category: ["Other"],
                value: [small[value].sum()],
                "_pct": [small["_pct"].sum()],
            })
            plot_data = pd.concat([big, other_row], ignore_index=True)
        else:
            plot_data = data

        colors = (self.theme.palette * (len(plot_data) // len(self.theme.palette) + 1))[:len(plot_data)]
        wedgeprops = dict(width=0.4) if donut else {}

        wedges, _texts, autotexts = ax.pie(
            plot_data[value],
            labels=plot_data[category],
            autopct=lambda p: f"{p:.1f}%" if p >= min_pct_label * 100 else "",
            colors=colors,
            wedgeprops=wedgeprops,
            pctdistance=0.8 if donut else 0.6,
            startangle=90,
            textprops={"fontsize": self.theme.label_font_size},
        )
        for at in autotexts:
            at.set_color("white")
            at.set_fontweight("bold")
            at.set_fontsize(self.theme.annotation_font_size)

        if donut:
            ax.text(0, 0, f"Total\n{_human_format(total)}", ha="center", va="center",
                    fontsize=self.theme.label_font_size + 1, fontweight="bold",
                    color=self.theme.text_color)

        ax.set_ylabel("")
        _title_block(fig, ax, self.theme, title, subtitle)

    def variance_waterfall(
        self, labels: Sequence[str], values: Sequence[float],
        title: str = "Variance Bridge", subtitle: Optional[str] = None,
        currency: Optional[str] = None, source: Optional[str] = None,
        total_label: str = "Total",
    ) -> Figure:
        """Waterfall chart showing sequential contributions to a total."""
        fig, ax = self._new_fig()
        n = len(values)
        cumulative = np.cumsum(values)
        starts = np.concatenate(([0], cumulative[:-1]))

        colors = []
        for v in values:
            if v >= 0:
                colors.append(self.theme.secondary_color)
            else:
                colors.append("#C1121F")
        colors[-1] = self.theme.primary_color  # total bar assumed last

        fmt = (lambda v: f"{currency}{_human_format(v)}") if currency else _human_format

        for i in range(n):
            base = 0 if i == n - 1 else starts[i]
            height = values[i] if i != n - 1 else cumulative[-2] if n > 1 else values[i]
            if i == n - 1:
                ax.bar(i, values[i], bottom=0, color=colors[i])
                label_y = values[i]
            else:
                ax.bar(i, values[i], bottom=starts[i], color=colors[i])
                label_y = starts[i] + values[i]
            ax.annotate(
                fmt(values[i]), (i, label_y),
                ha="center", va="bottom" if values[i] >= 0 else "top",
                fontsize=self.theme.annotation_font_size, xytext=(0, 3),

            if i < n - 1:

    def cohort_heatmap(

    def distribution(
        self, df: pd.DataFrame, value: str, group: Optional[str] = None,
        title: str = "Distribution", subtitle: Optional[str] = None,
        kind: str = "hist", source: Optional[str] = None,
    ) -> Figure:
        """Histogram/box/violin distribution chart with mean/median annotations."""
        fig, ax = self._new_fig()

        if kind == "hist":

        elif kind == "box":
            sns.boxplot(data=df, x=group, y=value, ax=ax,

                           palette=self.theme.palette if group else None,

        _title_block(fig, ax, self.theme, title, subtitle)
        _finalize(fig, ax, self.theme, source)

    def multi_series_trend(
        self, df: pd.DataFrame, x: str, y: str, series: str,

    # -- Output ----------------------------------------------------------

    def to_bytes(self, fig: Figure, fmt: str = "png") -> bytes:

        fig.savefig(buf, format=fmt, dpi=self.dpi, bbox_inches="tight",
